analysis: Divisor-closure, 300 random 2-variable laws (<= 4 leaves per side), N <= 9 with pruning - 251 laws have a model of some size 2..9 and 81 violate divisor-closure; violating pairs (N, d) - (8,2) 48, (6,3) 48, (6,2) 47, (9,3) 44, (4,2) 36, (8,4) 12; 9 laws with UNKNOWN instances. Example - ((xy)x)y = (y(xx))x has models at N = 6 and 8 but none at 2, 3, 4, 5. A first run (600 laws, N <= 10, budget 2,000,000) was stopped after 22 CPU-minutes.
assumptions: 300 laws sampled (seed 5) from the 2601 laws over {x,y} with at most 4 leaves per side (up to renaming and exchange of sides); a run with 600 laws, N <= 10 and budget 2,000,000 was stopped after 22 CPU-minutes (hard UNSAT instances at N = 9, 10)
sizes 2, 3, 5 always decided; a composite N in {4, 6, 8, 9} is decided only when one of its proper divisors is UNSAT (otherwise no violation is possible at N)
affine models decide SAT without a solver; conflict budget 200,000; UNKNOWN recorded
counterexamples: (xx)(xy) = y(y(yy)): models at N = 4, 6, 8 but not at N = 2
x(xy) = y(y(xx)): models at N = 5, 6, 8, 9 but not at 2, 3, 4

hypothesis: H-C13-1 (bold): every anchored spectrum is closed under divisors.
methodology: For each law: zero-substitution filter (N | m); affine roots; otherwise MagmaSAT with the anchor. Report every pair (N, d) with N SAT and d | N UNSAT.
question: Is there a law with an anchored model of some size N <= 9 but none of some size d | N?
